title: The General Ledger and Trial Balance
summary: Posting the CRJ, CPJ, DJ and CJ of a trading business to the General Ledger, the control accounts, balancing accounts, and drawing up a trial balance and knowing what it can and cannot show.

notes.caption: The accounting cycle: transactions on source documents are recorded in the journals, the journal totals are posted to the General Ledger, the accounts are balanced, and a trial balance checks the work.

notes.text: The **General Ledger** contains one account for each item. It is divided into the **Balance Sheet accounts section** (assets, liabilities and owner's equity) and the **Nominal accounts section** (income and expenses). At the end of each month the **column totals** of the journals are posted to the ledger.
Posting the journals of a trading business

notes.label: Remember
notes.text: Every transaction has a **debit** and an equal **credit** (the **double-entry principle**). That is why, if the posting is correct, the total of all debit balances equals the total of all credit balances.

**Debtors control** shows the total owed **to** the business by all its debtors. **Creditors control** shows the total the business owes **to** its creditors. Details for each individual customer or supplier are kept in the subsidiary **Debtors Ledger** and **Creditors Ledger**.

notes.caption: Debtors control (B6) of Lwazi Traders, June 2026

notes.title: Worked example 1: balancing Debtors control
notes.problem: Explain how the Debtors control account above was balanced.
steps: Add the bigger side (debit): 6 200 + 12 000 = 18 200. Write this total on both sides on the same line.
The difference, 18 200 − 8 800 = 9 400, is written on the credit side as 'Balance c/d' (carried down).
Bring the balance down on the opposite (debit) side on the first day of the next month as 'Balance b/d' (brought down).
notes.answer: Debtors owe Lwazi Traders R9 400 on 1 July: a debit balance, because Debtors control is an asset.

notes.text: A **trial balance** is a list of the **balances** of all the accounts in the General Ledger on a certain date. Debit balances go in the debit column and credit balances in the credit column. If the totals agree, the double entry has been done correctly.

notes.title: Worked example 2: finding a missing figure
notes.problem: A trial balance has debit balances of R84 300 and credit balances of R61 300 plus Capital, which is missing. Calculate Capital.
steps: The totals must be equal, so the credit total must also be R84 300.

notes.label: What a trial balance cannot show
notes.text: A trial balance can still balance when there are errors, for example if a transaction was **left out completely**, entered **twice**, posted to the **wrong account** on the correct side, or recorded with the **same wrong amount** on both sides.

questions.prompt: The CPJ of Lwazi Traders for July shows: Bank column R24 300; Trading stock R9 800; Wages R6 500; Creditors control R7 000; Sundry accounts: Rent expense R1 000. Explain how each total is posted to the General Ledger (name the account and side).
questions.memo:
✓ Bank R24 300 on the credit side of Bank (1)
✓ Trading stock R9 800 on the debit side of Trading stock (1)
✓ Wages R6 500 on the debit side of Wages (1)
✓ Creditors control R7 000 on the debit side of Creditors control (1)
✓ Rent expense R1 000 on the debit side of Rent expense (1)

questions.prompt: A learner's trial balance shows debit balances of R59 350 and credit balances of R60 250. She finds that Stationery of R450 was placed in the credit column. Explain why correcting this error makes the trial balance balance.
questions.memo:
✓ Stationery is an expense, so it has a debit balance (1)
✓ moving it to the debit column: debits R59 350 + R450 = R59 800 (1)
✓ credits R60 250 − R450 = R59 800, so the totals now agree (1)
